text: You're planning a trip, scrolling flight options, hunting for the best deal. All you want is to get there comfortably, without breaking the bank.
Then you spot it: a middle seat, significantly cheaper. You click 'book', feeling clever, only to immediately regret your squeezed-in choice.
Why do airlines even bother selling these cramped middle seats? You squeeze in, wondering if it's just a cruel trick for budget travelers.
It's not a trick. Airlines use 'price segmentation'. They know window and aisle seats have higher perceived value, so they price them accordingly.
The middle seat, lacking those perks, is a different product. It's sold cheaper to capture demand that prioritizes price, filling every possible space.
So while you pay less, you're paying with discomfort. You've traded legroom for a lower fare, now understanding the invisible system at play.
